detailed_reviews.precise_target: 两个子问：(a) 若 ω 是 quasi-transitive 图 G 上 a.s. 非空的 Aut(G)-不变 percolation，则 a.s. G 的每个 end 都含有 ω 的一个 end-convergent 子集；(b) 若 G 是 end 数大于 1 的 quasi-transitive 图，则 p_u(G) = 1。
detailed_reviews.printed_core: Comments 7.9 只给 (a)："Given ϵ > 0, let R be large enough that the balls of radius R satisfy P[B R (x) ∩ ω ̸= ∅] > 1 − ϵ for every vertex x. Since ϵ is arbitrary, the probability that K ∩ ω ̸= ∅ is actually 1. Since this holds for all finite F, the result follows."
detailed_reviews.unsupplied_parts: (b) 完全没有印刷文字；(a) 中由"每个 G\F 的无限分量与 ω 相交 a.s."过渡到"每个 end 含 end-convergent 子集"只用 "the result follows" 一句带过。

detailed_reviews.precise_target: 对任意图 G 证明两件事：(i) 谱半径满足 ρ(G) = lim_{n→∞} P_o[X_{2n} = o]^{1/2n}；(ii) 对所有 n 有 P_o[X_n = o] ≤ ρ(G)^n。
detailed_reviews.printed_core: "Solution 1. This follows from (6.13) and the proof of Proposition 6.6." "Solution 2. A direct proof goes as follows. ... Note that for any k and n, we have P o [X n = o] ≥ P o [X k = o] P o [X n−k = o] . Thus, by Fekete's lemma (Exercise 3.9), we have ρ(G) = lim n→∞ Po [X n = o]1/n as well as Po [Xn = o] ≤ ρ(G) n for all n. On the other hand, if Po [Xk = o] = 0 for odd k, it is still true that Po [Xk = o] is strictly positive for all even k, whence lim n→∞ Po [X2n = o]1/2n exists and equals ρ(G)." 另外 printed 261 印出被引用的定义 ρ(G) := lim sup_{n→∞} P_o[X_n = o]^{1/n}。

root_disagreements.comparison_basis: Stage-A levels were set from the blind question and Comment slices in runs/lyons-peres-ch7_1_14-review001/BLIND_INPUT.md and were not adjusted after the comparison; the stage-A rows are reproduced unchanged here apart from this key. What changed after stage A, stated plainly: the model pass that this run key exists for was in fact dispatched and completed - session 9e8dbaae-dfbc-479d-be3b-6e12ab870c6c, requested model deepseek-flash[1M], effort max, max_turns 1, num_turns 2, elapsed 501.7 s, exit_code 0, subtype success, framing complete_json_decoded, coverage 14 of 14, and four artifacts (CLAUDE_RAW_RESPONSE.json, TERMINAL.json, NATIVE_CONTROL.json, MODEL_RESULT.json) returned to runs/lyons-peres-ch7_1_14-review001/. Its 14 proposed levels are therefore a real third column in this comparison, not a re-reading by the same pass. The stage-A read_scope block was written while that run directory held BLIND_INPUT.md only, so its no_new_model: true records the stage-A state and not the state of the scope at the end; the top-level new_model_started_by_this_review records the latter. Independence: the model read only BLIND_INPUT.md, which is the question block and the Comment block and nothing else, so its levels were formed without the owner file in front of it. It is independent in input but not in operator, since the same session line wrote the stage-A file. Three columns are compared: stage A, the owner, and the model. The owner uses a finer vocabulary (H2, H2_material_incomplete_full_target, H1_retained_limited, H1_residual_recommendation), so literal strings differ from stage A on 11 of 14 keys; the model's literal strings differ from stage A on 6 of 14 (7.7, 7.8, 7.9, 7.10, 7.11, 7.14) and from the owner on all 14. Two things are compared: (i) whether a row sits in the H2 family, and (ii) whether the printed material is a countable complete H2. Only (i) is counted as a root disagreement. external_author_core_pending and H1_as_support_only are non-H2 labels for material whose core is outside the printed page. Stage A and the owner agree on family placement on all 14 keys: the same three rows (7.7, 7.9, 7.10) are H2-family on both sides, and the owner's own H2_core_complete flag is true for exactly 7.7 and 7.10. The model places all three of those rows outside the H2 family - H1 under action low_difficulty for 7.9 and 7.10, H1 under action external_author_core_pending for 7.7 - so the three root differences recorded below are stage A and owner against the model, not stage A against the owner. The model never asserts that a countable complete H2 exists anywhere in this scope, and on 7.9 it concedes the same material facts stage A records; its H1 is a difficulty tier proposed under the instruction to separate material state from difficulty. Whether a difficulty tier may overwrite a material-family placement is the question the adjudication has to answer; it is recorded here as open and is not settled in this file.
root_disagreements.countable_complete_H2_on_either_side: stage A: 7.7, 7.10 (both H2, both with a printed core covering the full stated target). owner: 7.7, 7.10 (both H2, H2_core_complete true). model: none - all fourteen proposals are H1 or the free-text 'none (external core unsupplied; research-level burden, no supplied author core)', and no H2 is proposed anywhere in this scope. 7.9 is H2-family for stage A and the owner with the core incomplete for the full target (part (b) has no author text) and H1/low_difficulty for the model; it is not a third countable core in any column.

h2_family_differences.deciding_printed_evidence: Comments 7.7, physical 638 (printed 621), lines 44-47: 'Let mu_omega2 and nu_omega2 be the conditional distributions of omega1 and omega3 given omega2. Then let (omega1, omega2, omega3) have the law where (omega1, omega3) has conditional law mu_omega2 x nu_omega2 given omega2. See Exercise 18.20 of Billingsley (1995) for a general construction from specified conditional distributions. One can also make a similar construction for finite A and then use Kolmogorov's existence theorem.' The recombination that produces a monotone triple is printed; what is not printed is the existence theorem for a joint law with prescribed conditional kernels, which the author replaces with two named routes.
h2_family_differences.why_this_is_a_root_difference: The model pass records action external_author_core_pending with proposed_level H1, and its own concrete_remaining_burden says the residual is technical because 'the existence of a regular conditional distribution and of a joint law with the prescribed conditional kernels rests on the cited general construction, which is not supplied'. Stage A and the owner both treat the cited construction as the author's disposal of that step and keep the row in the H2 family. The two labels measure different things - the model's measures residual weight, stage A's measures whether an author core for the stated target is printed - but the model's action string denies that the author core is supplied, so the family placement genuinely differs and is counted here rather than smoothed into a label-only difference.
h2_family_differences.owner_own_text_supports_the_printed_core: Yes, with a qualifier the owner already carries. The owner's concrete_core is the same conditional-on-middle-variable recombination, and its remaining_gap is only 'Verifying that the recombined law has marginals P1, P2, P3 and that its support sits inside the ordering set. Both are immediate from the construction; nothing beyond the cited tool is missing.' The owner also records its own confidence for this row as medium and warns that if the check 'is held to be substantive rather than immediate, this row falls to H2_material_incomplete_full_target' - which is a fall, not a move out of the H2 family.

h2_family_differences.deciding_printed_evidence: Comments 7.9, physical 638 (printed 621), lines 49-52, argue part (a) only: the epsilon-R ball step, 'every infinite component K of G minus F contains a ball of radius R and therefore intersects omega with probability more than 1 - epsilon', closing with 'Since this holds for all finite F, the result follows.' Part (b), p_u(G) = 1 for quasi-transitive G with more than one end, has no printed line anywhere in the Comments block.
h2_family_differences.why_this_is_a_root_difference: The model pass gives action low_difficulty with proposed_level H1, and its own concrete_remaining_burden concedes both stage-A facts: the hint 'does not deliver the passage from every infinite component of G minus F meets omega to an actual end-convergent subset inside a prescribed end', and 'part (b) has no supplied proof material at all'. So the disagreement is not about the printed page but about what H1 means here: the model files a row whose target is half unprinted as low difficulty, while stage A and the owner file it in the H2 family with the core incomplete. It is counted as a family difference for that reason; the material facts are identical across all three columns.
h2_family_differences.owner_own_text_supports_the_printed_core: Yes. The owner's owner_reason_for_downgrade is 'The printed argument is complete for (a) but the target has two parts. A complete core for the full target is therefore not supplied', and its remaining_gap is 'The whole of (b).' The owner's H2_core_complete flag is false here, so the owner does not claim a second countable core.

h2_family_differences.deciding_printed_evidence: Comments 7.10, physical 638-639 (printed 621-622), print two solutions. Solution 1: 'This follows from (6.13) and the proof of Proposition 6.6.' Solution 2 prints the supermultiplicativity display 'P_o[X_n = o] >= P_o[X_k = o] P_o[X_{n-k} = o]', then 'Thus, by Fekete's lemma (Exercise 3.9), we have rho(G) = lim_{n} P_o[X_n = o]^{1/n} as well as P_o[X_n = o] <= rho(G)^n for all n', and the parity sentence 'if P_o[X_k = o] = 0 for odd k, it is still true that P_o[X_k = o] is strictly positive for all even k, whence lim P_o[X_{2n} = o]^{1/2n} exists and equals rho(G)'. Both requested statements are covered by printed steps; the only inputs not printed on these pages are Fekete's lemma, (6.13) and Proposition 6.6, all three inside the same book.
h2_family_differences.why_this_is_a_root_difference: The model pass gives action low_difficulty with proposed_level H1, remarking that 'the residual work is verifying Fekete's lemma and identifying the limit with the spectral radius, both printed or standard'. That remark agrees with the printed page; what differs is the tier. Stage A and the owner both read a fully printed direct proof of both requested statements as H2 material. Counted as a family difference because the same printed evidence is placed in different families by columns that both claim to be reading the same slices.
h2_family_differences.owner_own_text_supports_the_printed_core: Yes. The owner's concrete_core is 'Supermultiplicativity of the return probabilities plus Fekete's lemma, applied to the full sequence in the aperiodic case and to the even subsequence in the periodic case, which is exactly the dichotomy that the definition of rho(G) as a limsup needs in order to become a limit', and its remaining_gap is 'Supplying the one-sentence positivity claim for even times, and restating the bound in the periodic case. Both are mechanical given the printed display.'
